simple: After you make or pick an animation, you need scripts to actually use it in your game. This page shows two things: playing an animation from a script (like a kick when a player presses a key) and swapping out the default character animations (like replacing the normal run with a Ninja Run). It also lists the asset IDs for Roblox's catalog animation packs, such as Ninja, Robot, Zombie, and Superhero. With this, your characters can move in their own style.
analogy: An animation asset is like a dance video saved online. The `Animation` object is the link, `LoadAnimation` is pressing "download" onto your character, and `Play()` is pressing the play button.
keyPoints: To play an animation on a character: get the `Animator` inside the `Humanoid`, create an `Animation` with an `AnimationId`, load it with `Animator:LoadAnimation()` to get an `AnimationTrack`, then call `:Play()`.
Rigs without a `Humanoid` need an `AnimationController` with an `Animator` inside it before you can load animations.
You can listen for named animation events on the track with `GetMarkerReachedSignal`.
To replace default animations, use a Script in ServerScriptService that changes the `AnimationId` values inside each character's `Animate` script, like `animateScript.run.RunAnim.AnimationId`.
The page's replace script first stops all playing tracks with `GetPlayingAnimationTracks()` and `:Stop(0)`, and runs on `CharacterAppearanceLoaded`.
Default animations you can replace include run, walk, jump, idle (two versions), fall, swim, swim idle, and climb.
When there are multiple versions (like two idles), `Weight` controls how often each plays: weight divided by the total weight.
Catalog pack IDs are listed on the page. For example, Ninja Run is `656118852` and Ninja Jump is `656117878`.

terms.Animation: An object that just holds the asset ID of an animation. It does not play by itself.
terms.AnimationId: The address of the animation, written as `rbxassetid://` plus the number, like `rbxassetid://656118852`.
terms.Animator: The object inside a `Humanoid` or `AnimationController` that loads and plays animations.
terms.AnimationTrack: What you get after loading an animation. It has `Play()`, `Stop()`, and signals you can use.
terms.AnimationController: Used instead of a `Humanoid` for rigs that are not characters, like a moving machine or a creature without a Humanoid.
terms.Animate script: The script Roblox puts inside every player character that plays default animations like walking and jumping.
terms.weight: How likely one version is to be picked. With Animation1 weight 5 and Animation2 weight 10, the total is 15, so Animation1 plays 5/15 = one third of the time and Animation2 two thirds.
terms.catalog: Roblox's shop of avatar items, including animation packs.
terms.comment out: Putting `--` in front of a line so it does not run. Removing `--` is called uncommenting.

example.title: Kick when you press F
example.code:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local animator = humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator")

-- The Animation object holds the asset ID
local kickAnimation = Instance.new("Animation")
kickAnimation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://2515090838"

-- Load once so we get a reusable AnimationTrack
local kickTrack = animator:LoadAnimation(kickAnimation)

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
	-- Ignore keys typed into chat or text boxes
	if gameProcessed then
		return
	end
	if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.F then
		kickTrack:Play()
	end
end)
explain: The script sits in the character, so `script.Parent` is the character.
We wait for the `Humanoid` and its `Animator`.
We make an `Animation` and give it the kick's asset ID from the page.
`LoadAnimation` gives us `kickTrack`. We load it once at the start, not on every key press.
When the player presses F (and is not typing in chat), we call `kickTrack:Play()`.

watchOut: Calling `LoadAnimation` on the `Humanoid` instead of the `Animator`. Use `humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator")` and load on that.
Forgetting `rbxassetid://` in front of the ID number.
Using an animation you do not own or that is not shared with your game or group. It will not play.
Custom replacements for default animations need the final keyframe named `End` when you publish them.
Animations with low priority can be hidden by default ones. Set a higher priority (like Action) in the Animation Editor for things like attacks.
